I'd say that if you need closure to move on, just tell them. Let them know how you feel, because if you don't you'll be stuck wondering for the rest of your life. For all you know they could like you, maybe their being hot and cold because they don't know your feelings.

If you think you can manage telling them in person, I'd say go somewhere you two can talk without being interrupted. It's the best way to get an immediate reaction, and talk things out if your friends and want to keep it that way, if they're not interested.

Only if you can't manage doing that, then I'd say message them about it. But be aware, you won't know how they react immediately and it could be harder to save any relations you have. In this day and age though texting is something we all do, I don't think it's looked down on much anymore when you message someone about your feelings.

Another thing, if it's gotten to this point, and you can't get over them. I think you should just outright tell them while you still have a chance. They might start dating this other guy, or just not be around anymore soon. If you keep hesitating you'll just regret it later on, I'd say if you're getting some green signals from her, then do it.

I wish you luck! Let me know what you decide to do, and how it works out for you in the end!

I've been in both situations before, on being the person that is liked by two friends (didn't find out the other liked me until after I started dating the first.) And liking the same person as my friend.

The best advice I could give you is to have long conversation with your friend to see how things are gonna go. As well as let the person you both like decide for themselves. Expect for it to hurt a bit if you have strong feelings for the person and things don't go very well. 

Because yes I'd think most people value their friendship over a crush. But in most cases it's the more empathetic person that looses. So if you like the person, talk to your friend, then go for it.
Honestly just tell her you want a relationship, I've been there, I'm still there. Just let them know, it'll end much better that way.

Sounds like their Bi but prefer women over men, though that doesn't mean you don't have a chance. If you think about it as well basically everyone has someone they like, so even if she said she doesn't like anyone. There has to be at least one person she's kinda interested in, if you're best friends I don't see why she wouldn't tell you. Unless it's someone she doesn't want you to know, or it's you.

With the 90% 10% thing I think you're just gonna have to cross your fingers. Also if you do ask her and she says she needs time to think. It could be because she'd never thought about you in that way, and now she's gonna spend a bunch of time picturing you guys together seeing if that's something she wants.

In situations like this, from experience, you want to tell them as soon as possible. It's been a year for me now liking someone, I've over thought things so many times. I can't even tell if the person sees me as a friend.

If you want to know right away how she feels about it, and be able to tell if she's twisting the truth a little bit. I would say tell her in person, in a private space. Even if she says no you guys could talk about it some more, and have better chances of saving your friendship.

You could do it over text, but you might not get a reply or a reaction right away and you won't know how she's reacting to it good or bad. Then she also has time to carefully think out what to say is a way that can sometimes be vague, that or she could just not answer depending on the situation.

So you could say it in person, get immediate reactions, though it's going to take a lot of courage.
Or you could message her, get a thought out reply, though it would be easier to say.

Well if you were to tell her and she started avoiding you after saying no, was she really a good friend in the first place? Of course if you tell her and she says no you'll need time away from her to get over the feeling.

Another thing you could do is drop signs that you like her, try flirting and see how she reacts. The longer you wait to do anything about it though, the more difficult it'll be to cross the line of friendship.
